name: Wind Power IoT Platform
tagline: Real-time turbine monitoring across 8 wind farms
background: Built from zero to one for a wind-power customer support team managing roughly 2TB of turbine manuals, troubleshooting guides, and maintenance records. The product turned fragmented device documentation into a retrieval workflow that operators could trust during live support sessions.

technicalDecisions.title: Chunking and retrieval tuned for equipment manuals
technicalDecisions.explanation: Split long PDF manuals into section-aware chunks keyed by device model, subsystem, and failure code so retrieval stayed precise even when the source corpus mixed scanned files, SOPs, and revision-heavy documentation.

technicalDecisions.title: Trust-first answer rendering
technicalDecisions.explanation: Structured every response around citations, source snippets, and document provenance to keep customer support agents inside an auditable workflow instead of relying on opaque model output.

technicalDecisions.title: Streaming chat with controlled latency
technicalDecisions.explanation: Used SSE-based streaming responses and staged retrieval so operators could start reading an answer quickly while the system completed reranking and evidence assembly in the background.

name: Gate SEO Platform
tagline: Performance-first SEO analytics for a top-10 crypto exchange
background: Led a dedicated SEO rebuild for Gate's large data-content surfaces, including liquidation feeds, capital-flow dashboards, and other traffic-heavy pages. The project replaced a CSR-only delivery model with a crawlable, performance-focused architecture built for search growth at scale.

technicalDecisions.title: CSR to SSR migration with short-cycle caching
technicalDecisions.explanation: Chose Next.js server rendering with controlled revalidation instead of static generation because the underlying market data changed minute by minute and still needed indexable HTML for search engines.

technicalDecisions.title: Structured data as a ranking multiplier
technicalDecisions.explanation: Systematically injected JSON-LD for dataset and financial content pages to improve Google understanding of page intent and unlock richer result surfaces beyond standard blue links.

technicalDecisions.title: Performance budgets tied to SEO rollout
technicalDecisions.explanation: Treated LCP, CLS, and layout stability as release gates so search visibility gains would not come at the cost of user-perceived speed on mobile-heavy traffic.

name: Michaels Design System
tagline: Shared frontend foundation across four retail product lines
background: Served as frontend tech lead for Michaels across MakerPlace, Rewards, Classes, and store experiences, aligning multiple product lines on a shared component system and delivery model. The work focused on making multi-team execution faster without fragmenting UX or performance standards.

technicalDecisions.title: Token architecture layered from global to component scope
technicalDecisions.explanation: Built the system on top of Chakra UI with global, semantic, and component-level token layers so teams could reuse primitives while still supporting product-level theme adaptation.

technicalDecisions.title: Multi-format package output for broad adoption
technicalDecisions.explanation: Used Rollup multi-entry builds to ship ESM and CJS packages with tree-shaking support, keeping the design system consumable across older storefront apps and newer feature teams.

technicalDecisions.title: Migration strategy paired with performance work
technicalDecisions.explanation: Combined the design system rollout with SSR-friendly Vite migration and dependency slimming so shared components improved consistency without becoming a performance tax.

name: Chaos Developer Platform
background: Built for a bank's core systems to support fault-injection experiments, real-time observability, and resilience governance in a financial-grade environment. The product needed to make complex experiment design safe enough for daily engineering use.

technicalDecisions.title: Graph-based experiment editor instead of form-only configuration
technicalDecisions.explanation: Used AntV/X6 to model failure nodes, dependency paths, and execution order visually, cutting experiment setup time while making propagation risks much easier to inspect before launch.

technicalDecisions.title: High-frequency rendering pipeline for observability views
technicalDecisions.explanation: Combined data windowing, requestAnimationFrame scheduling, and Canvas-based charts to keep dashboards responsive under roughly 2,000 updates per second.

technicalDecisions.title: Report distribution built into the workflow
technicalDecisions.explanation: Integrated PDF export, share links, and multi-chart reporting directly into experiment results so reliability reviews could move faster than manual screenshot-based handoffs.
